quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale:
The rule is satisfied at the preferred position. Section 14 (p0079) gives Client (Mortgage Logic.com) an unconditional termination-for-convenience right exercisable by written notice, with services continuing only until the last day of the month following the notice month — an effective notice period of roughly 30 to 60 days, at or better than the preferred 30 days and well inside the 60–90 day fallback. No cause, consent, or justification is required, and no early-termination fee, penalty, or accelerated-fee clawback is imposed anywhere in the agreement.

Direction is also correct on the Vendor side: TrueLink has no termination-for-convenience right during the committed term. Its only exit routes are for-cause termination of Sections 2 and 3 upon Client breach or a Credit Repository/System Agreement default (p0078), and symmetrical non-renewal at the end of a one-year period. The term is a 1-year initial term auto-renewing in one-year increments (p0078), so there is no multi-year commitment and no walk-away exposure.

Two minor sub-elements fall short of the model language but are not material deviations and are not flagged. First, there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; this is functionally moot because Section 5a (p0045) has TrueLink invoice monthly with payment due within 15 days of receipt, so fees are paid in arrears and no prepayment accrues to be refunded. Second, the Vendor's end-of-term non-renewal notice is 30 days rather than the fallback's 90 days, but this is a non-renewal of a one-year term rather than a mid-term convenience termination, and the right is symmetrical — it is equally available to us, so we would not trade for a longer period here.

Two drafting notes worth raising in negotiation but not by redline under this rule: Section 13's cross-reference to "Section 12" for termination is a mis-numbering (termination lives in Section 14, and Section 12 is the indemnity), and the "Subject to Section 4 hereof" carve-out in Section 14 points to the Support Services minimum commitment period, which is left blank ("not less than ____ months") at p0043. We should ensure that blank is filled at a figure we are comfortable with, since it could otherwise be argued to qualify our convenience right as to Support Services.

Noted only for awareness: § 8.f lets TrueLink "implement technical mechanisms" to prevent spamming, but that is an enforcement measure on TrueLink's own Interface rather than an audit or inspection of Client's systems or records, and it is addressed under the acceptable-use rules rather than here.

quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
rationale: There is a minimum commitment on us: Section 5(a) sets a monthly floor ("not less than $____ per month") for Hosting and Support Services, and Section 6 makes those minimum monthly fees non-contestable. However, the commitment sits at the playbook fallback rather than in walk-away territory: (i) exposure is confined to the current 12-month term, since Section 13 runs for one year and renews in one-year increments subject to 30 days' notice of non-renewal by either party; (ii) Section 14 gives us a stand-alone right to terminate at any time on written notice, with services (and therefore the minimum) ending the last day of the month following notice — roughly a 30-60 day exit; and (iii) there is no shortfall payment, penalty or accelerated-balance mechanic anywhere in the document, so we pay only monthly minimums for months actually served. Section 2(a) also confirms we are "not obligated to utilize the License" and may source equivalent services elsewhere, so there is no volume cap or exclusivity backing the floor. Two drafting points to note but not redline: the dollar amounts and the Section 4 support period are left blank and should be completed before signature, and Section 6's reference to "the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" is a mis-cross-reference (the minimums are in Section 5(a)); Section 14's "Subject to Section 4" should likewise be confirmed as preserving TrueLink's support-availability period rather than qualifying our termination right.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
rationale: The renewal mechanic sits in the Term clause (Section 13, p0078): the initial term is 1 year and the Agreement renews automatically for successive one-year periods, with either party — including us as Client — able to prevent renewal on written notice given no later than 30 days before the end of the then-current year. On the material terms this meets the preferred position: renewal terms are 12 months (not multi-year), and the non-renewal notice window is 30 days, well inside both the preferred 30-day and fallback 60-day limits, and nowhere near the 90-day walk-away threshold. The notice right is mutual, so it does not operate against us. Two preferred sub-elements are absent and are noted only: there is no Vendor obligation to send a renewal reminder 60 days ahead, and there is no CPI/3% cap on renewal price increases — Section 6 (p0047) only freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year and adds a most-favoured-rate commitment, leaving uplift at renewal uncapped. If the renewal pricing is negotiated elsewhere, we may raise the uplift cap as a low-priority ask alongside the fee schedule rather than under this rule.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added an exit clause requiring TrueLink, on expiry or termination, to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our Content and Credit Data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and then delete and certify deletion. As TrueLink hosts our Web Site and borrower data, the Agreement currently gives us no right to get that data back or to migrate in an orderly way; we can accept a 90-day assistance period if six months is difficult.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates, including reasonable assistance in migrating the Web Site, Client Content and Client's data to Client or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days of Client's request, return to Client all Client Content, Credit Data and other data and materials of Client then in TrueLink's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such Client Content, Credit Data and other data and materials from its systems and backup media and certify such deletion to Client in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance, data return in machine-readable format, and certified deletion into Section 14 (Termination).

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: This is a web site hosting and support agreement under which TrueLink hosts our Web Site, Client Content, backups (Section 2(f)) and borrower/loan Credit Data, so the rule expects an exit clause. None exists. Section 14 only obliges TrueLink to keep providing Hosting and Support Services until the last day of the month following our termination notice — roughly 30-60 days of continued service, not transition or migration assistance. Section 13 (p0078) confirms we retain ownership of domains and Client Content and gives us 30/60 days to arrange a new name server and hosting environment, but it places that burden entirely on us and imposes no obligation on TrueLink to return, export or delete our data. Section 10 (Confidentiality) contains no return-or-destroy provision at all, so even that partial substitute is absent, and searches for return/export/delete/destroy/transition produced no relevant provision. The fallback (90 days' assistance plus data export within 30 days) therefore also fails. Inserted the preferred position into Section 14: up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Client Content and Credit Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification. Placement in Section 14 is effective post-termination because Section 24 (p0090) provides that Sections 1 and 5 through 30 survive expiration or termination. We would accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: 30. FORCE MAJEURE. TrueLink will be excused from delays in performing or from failing to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent the delays or failures result from causes beyond the reasonable control or TrueLink.
rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no hits and the outline contains no insurance heading; the miscellaneous provisions run from Section 13 through Section 30 (Force Majeure) and then straight to the signature block, so no insurance covenant exists anywhere in the Agreement. This is material rather than a drafting nicety because TrueLink is a hosting vendor: it hosts the Web Site, receives and uploads Client Content (§ 1.b), and transmits and archives Credit Data consisting of borrower and loan-applicant credit information from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian (§ 1.d). A vendor processing personal financial data with no insurance at all is walk-away territory under the rule, and neither the preferred nor the fallback position (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is met. The gap is not cured elsewhere: TrueLink's indemnity in § 12.b is unsupported by any coverage requirement, and § 12 caps its liability for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 at 12 months' hosting and support fees, so we have no funded backstop for a data incident. Proposed new Section 31 inserted after § 30, before the signature block, with the preferred package — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request — using the Agreement's own defined terms (Client Content, Credit Data). The fallback of E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M is offered in the comment if TrueLink pushes back on limits.
